docs.title: 1. Memory Requirements
docs.text:
RNNs vs Transformers: - RNNs: Lower memory (sequential processing) - Transformers: Higher memory (self-attention is O(n²)) - Bidirectional models: ~2x parameters of unidirectional

Implications: - Adjust batch sizes per architecture - LSTM can use larger batches than BERT/GPT-2

docs.title: 2. Training Speed
docs.text: Relative Speed (approximate): - Unidirectional LSTM: Fastest (sequential) - Bidirectional LSTM: 2x slower (two passes) - GPT-2: Medium (parallelizable) - BERT: Slowest (bidirectional attention + MLM)

docs.title: 3. Generation Capability
docs.text:
Supports Autoregressive Generation: - ✅ GPT-2 (designed for it) - ✅ Unidirectional LSTM (natural fit) - ❌ BERT (not designed for generation) - ⚠️ Bidirectional LSTM (possible but awkward)

Implications for Evaluation: - Some evaluations (BLIMP) require adaptation for BERT - Need pseudo-perplexity for bidirectional models

docs.title: 4. Checkpoint Compatibility
docs.text:
HuggingFace Compatibility: - GPT-2: Full compatibility - BERT: Full compatibility - LSTM: Custom implementation, need custom loading

Implications: - Can load pretrained GPT-2/BERT from HuggingFace - LSTM models trained from scratch only

docs.title: Code Changes (Estimated Lines of Code)
docs.text:
New Code: - Architecture abstraction: ~500 lines - BERT implementation: ~200 lines - LSTM implementation: ~400 lines - Data collators: ~200 lines - Tokenizer factory: ~300 lines - Total new code: ~1600 lines

Modified Code: - Config updates: ~200 lines - Model factory: ~100 lines - Trainer updates: ~50 lines - Data processor: ~100 lines - Total modifications: ~450 lines

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: New Python Packages: - tokenizers (HuggingFace tokenizers library) - already likely installed - No additional dependencies needed

docs.title: Testing Requirements
docs.text:
Unit Tests: - Test each architecture creates successfully - Test model registry - Test data collators - Test tokenizer types

Integration Tests: - End-to-end training for each architecture - Evaluation compatibility - Checkpoint saving/loading

Performance Tests: - Memory usage profiling - Training speed benchmarks - Convergence validation

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Expanding model_foundry to support RNN, LSTM, and BERT is feasible and well-scoped:

  1. Clean Abstraction: Registry pattern keeps architectures modular
  2. Minimal Core Changes: Most existing code remains untouched
  3. Backwards Compatible: Existing GPT-2 experiments continue working
  4. Incremental: Can implement architectures one at a time
  5. Well-Tested: HuggingFace integration provides validation

Estimated Effort: 6 weeks for full implementation with testing

Key Benefits: - Compare architectural inductive biases on same data - Study how RNNs vs Transformers learn linguistic phenomena - Investigate bidirectional vs unidirectional processing - Unified pipeline for all experiments

Recommended Approach: Implement in phases, maintaining backwards compatibility throughout.

docs.title: Gemini Project Charter: Subject-Drop Rearing Study
docs.text: This document outlines the core principles, architecture, and workflow for the "Just drop the subject" experimental framework. Its purpose is to provide context and guide future development and interaction.

docs.title: 1. Project Goal & Intentions
docs.text:
The primary objective of this project is to conduct a controlled rearing study to investigate the acquisition of grammatical rules in Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically focusing on subject-drop phenomena in English.

The experimental methodology involves:

  • Dataset: Training on the BabyLM dataset, a 100-million-word corpus designed to be developmentally plausible.
  • Interventions: Performing a series of linguistic ablations on the training corpus to create controlled experimental conditions (e.g., removing expletives, impoverishing morphology).
  • Measurement: Evaluating model performance using surprisal on minimal linguistic pairs and general competence with the BLIMP benchmark.

docs.title: 2. Core Design Principles
docs.text:
The codebase is built on the following principles to ensure a robust, scalable, and reproducible research environment:

  • Configuration-Driven: Every aspect of an experiment (data, ablations, model hyperparameters, training procedure) is defined in a single, human-readable .yaml file. The code is merely an engine that executes the plan laid out in the config. This makes experiments easy to define, track, and share.
  • Modularity: The codebase is strictly divided into logical components: data preparation, linguistic preprocessing, tokenization, model training, and evaluation. Each component is independent and can be run separately.
  • Reproducibility: By combining a configuration-driven approach with a fixed random seed, any experiment can be perfectly replicated. The .yaml file is the single source of truth for an entire experimental pipeline.
  • Scalability: The framework is designed to handle large corpora by processing files in memory-efficient streams and chunks, rather than loading entire datasets at once.

docs.title: 3. Codebase Architecture & Workflow
docs.text: The project is organized into a well-defined filesystem and is operated through a modular Command Line Interface (CLI).

docs.title: 3.1. Filesystem Structure
docs.text:
.
├── configs/              # Experiment definition files (.yaml)
├── data/                 # Raw, processed, and evaluation datasets
├── preprocessing/        # Scripts for linguistic ablations
├── tokenizers/           # Trained tokenizer models for each experiment
├── models/               # Saved model checkpoints
├── model_foundry/        # The core Python source code package
│   ├── cli.py            # Main CLI entrypoint (using Typer)
│   ├── config.py         # Pydantic models for validating configs
│   └── ...
├── evaluation/           # Scripts for post-training analysis
├── .gitignore
├── pyproject.toml
└── README.md

docs.title: 3.2. Modular CLI Workflow
docs.text:
The entire experimental pipeline is executed through a series of independent commands, making it ideal for managing resources on a compute cluster.

  1. Define Experiment: Create a new .yaml file in configs/.
  2. Prepare Corpus (One-Time Setup): 
    python preprocessing/00_prepare_corpus.py --source_dir <...> --main_output_dir <...> --pool_output_dir <...>
  3. Run Linguistic Ablations: 
    python preprocessing/remove_expletives.py --input_dir <...> --output_dir <...> --replacement_pool_dir <...>
  4. Train Tokenizer: 
    python -m model_foundry.cli train-tokenizer configs/your_experiment.yaml
  5. Train Model: 
    python -m model_foundry.cli run configs/your_experiment.yaml
  6. Evaluate Model: 
    python -m evaluation.surprisal --checkpoint_path <...> --stimuli_file <...>

docs.title: Training-Stack Optimization Audit
docs.text:
Date: 2026-06-04

Produced by a 64-agent adversarially-verified audit workflow; 33 suggestions confirmed / 21 refuted.

Adopted items are tracked in docs/design_ledger.md.

I have all the data I need to synthesize the report. Let me write it directly.

docs.title: Training-Stack Optimization Audit — Clean Re-Run of the 300-Run English Production Matrix
docs.text: This report synthesizes finder suggestions and adversarial-verifier verdicts. Where a verifier overrode a finder, the verifier's adjusted gain and science tag are used. Only suggestions with is_real=true appear in sections 1–3; killed suggestions are in section 4.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary — Top 5 Fleet-Wide Levers by Verified Wall-Clock Impact
docs.text:
1. Route gpt2_large + bert_large to A100-80GB (if reservation access is confirmed) — ~3–4x per-run throughput; ~590 GPU-days → ~200–295 GPU-days for the heavy block (~295–390 GPU-days saved). GATED: the "no reservation needed" claim contradicts repo ground truth (CLAUDE.md:182,228); confirm admin-granted access first or it is a policy violation / 0 gain.
  2. Disable gradient checkpointing on the GPT-2 family (small/medium/large) — ~25% per-step reduction; for gpt2_large that is ~16.5 s/step off a ~66 s/step run, ~60–70 GPU-h/run. Note: GC is already a silent no-op for Mamba and BERT (no method exposed), so it yields nothing there. Provably identical math.
  3. Enable torch.compile / Inductor in the production base configs — ~8–18% per-step on the GPT-2/BERT transformer subset (gated down from 10–25% by active gradient checkpointing + no drop_last recompiles). One-line config flip (compile_mode: 'default'); the torch._dynamo.disable() at trainer.py:198 is a no-op and need NOT be removed. Tens of GPU-days matrix-wide. Tag: validate numerical parity.
  4. Raise per-cell parallelism 2 → 4–6 for light archs — collapses the calendar tail: a 10-completion cell drains in ~2 waves instead of 5 (~2.5x ceiling per cell). Adds zero GPU-days, does not trip the NRP webhook (per-pod request unchanged). Realized end-to-end gain is single-digit-days, bounded by the slowest pod per cell.
  5. Stratify the heavy/long-pole archs off the slow L4 tier (soft preference toward 3090/4090) — rescues any run that would have landed on L4 from up to ~3x slowdown back to ~1x; per-cell makespan ~1.3–1.6x. Launcher-only nodeAffinity change. PI design decision (shifts seed-vs-node confound).

docs.title: gpt2_small
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Soft-prefer fast 24GB cards (3090/4090), keep L4 as fallback Per-run: up to ~1.5–1.66x on the ~25–33% of runs that hit L4; matrix makespan uncertain/possibly neutral Low (launcher nodeAffinity) design_decision

Use lever (b), a preferredDuringScheduling weight, not a hard L4 exclusion — hard exclusion removes ~25% of the pool and the matrix is concurrency-bound, so net makespan is ambiguous. Note gpt2_small is ~40 EN runs, not 240.

docs.title: gpt2_medium
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Disable gradient checkpointing (this config is a 124M GPT-2-small-footprint model) ~12–20% wall-clock Low (config flag) safe Enable torch.compile / Inductor ~8–15% per-step (FA2 already handles attention; Inductor fuses pointwise/LN/GELU) Low (config flip) needs_resweep* Raise phys batch 16 → 32 at constant eff batch ~2–6% (favor 32 over 64; schedule-shift risk grows) Low safe Switch fp16 → bf16 AMP ~0–1% wall-clock; real value is stability Medium (plumb dtype) needs_resweep Per-arch GPU pool stratification (drop/soft-prefer off L4) Tail-bounded; median unchanged, up to ~3x on L4-landing runs Low design_decision Async checkpoint writes + relocate empty_cache() ~sub-1% to ~3%; true write volume ~120–190 GB/run (355M model) Medium safe

*Inductor is safe if a 1-seed loss-curve check matches eager; the verifier tagged the medium variant as falling under the standard compile caveat. The cross-cutting compile finding (§3) is needs_resweep pending parity validation.

docs.title: gpt2_large
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Disable gradient checkpointing (354M, gpt2-medium sizing — fits ~9.7 GB at phys 4) ~0.78–0.80x → ~4.5 GPU-days/run, saving ~1.1–1.4 GPU-days/run Low (config flag) safe A100-80GB reservation (3–4x + 80GB headroom for no-ckpt phys 32) 5.73 → ~1.6–1.9 GPU-days/run; single largest per-run lever Medium (toleration/affinity) design_decision Enable torch.compile / Inductor ~0.85–0.90x realized (10–15% likely), ~0.57–0.86 GPU-days/run; medium confidence (graph-breaks possible) Low needs_resweep Switch fp16 → bf16 AMP ~0.97–1.0x (≤0.1 GPU-day/run); robustness, not speed Medium needs_resweep

Note the largest gpt2_large win is the A100 move, but it is gated on confirming nautilus.io/reservation access — the 5.73→0.49 GPU-day matrix-wide figure is inconsistent with the recommendation (route only gpt2_large + bert_large), ignore it.

docs.title: bert_large
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Stratify off L4 (BERT_POOL of 3090/A10/4090; mirror the mamba sub-pool pattern) Per-run tail rescue: ~21 → ~6 GPU-days for any L4-bound run; slice-mean ~15–25% at a plausible 10–15% L4 fraction (upper-plausible, not established) Low (one launcher list edit) design_decision Remove/fix the dead use_gradient_checkpointing: true flag (silent no-op on BERT wrapper) ~0 direct; prevents a ~25–33% recompute regression if someone "fixes" it Low (config honesty) safe Enable torch.compile / Inductor ~5–12% per run, and ONLY if GC made compile-compatible; else 0–5% or regression Low–Medium needs_resweep*

*Verifier downgraded the BERT compile finding to is_real=false on its stated "two defeaters" premise (the dynamo.disable is a no-op), but the underlying lever survives via the cross-cutting compile finding (§3); treat BERT compile gain as ~5–12% conditional on GC. BERT uses SDPA, not FA2.

docs.title: lstm
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Move LSTM off the 24GB pool onto A4000 (16GB) / MIG slices Per-run compute unchanged (~9h); matrix-level: frees 24GB slots + cuts queue-behind-transformer latency; magnitude unquantifiable from code Low–Medium (net-new affinity plumbing) design_decision Avoid the redundant ~1.6 GB contiguous() copy of shifted logits (slice rnn_output[:, :-1] BEFORE the projection) ~1–3% per run (up to ~5–8% on slow A10/L4); LSTM-only Low–Medium (re-check logits-shape consumers) safe Confirm torch.compile stays OFF for LSTM (cuDNN already fused) 0 (prevents wasted plumbing effort) None safe Bump CPU 2 → 4 for >1 dataloader worker + persistent_workers Conditional/measurement-gated; 5% data_fraction = ~27 min/run, 10% = ~53 min/run IF data-bound; possibly ~0 if prefetch already hides it Low (gated on telemetry + NRP webhook) safe

Realize the contiguous-copy fix via the pre-projection slice, NOT a .reshape swap (reshape still copies). The finder's own "3–6 min/run" CPU-worker figure was arithmetically wrong (too low); use the data_fraction-gated estimate.

docs.title: mamba_370m
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Stratify Mamba to fast 24GB cards (drop/soft-prefer off L4) Per L4-bound run up to ~3x; per-cell makespan ~1.3–1.6x; fleet gain scales with L4 frequency Low (MAMBA_POOL already plumbed) design_decision Remove the misleading use_gradient_checkpointing: true flag (silent no-op on Mamba wrapper) ~0 (honesty fix; do NOT implement real GC — it would slow training) Low safe Switch fp16 → bf16 AMP ~0–1% wall-clock; stability/de-risking, not throughput Medium needs_resweep torch.compile the pointwise glue (fullgraph=False around custom kernels) ~0–3%, conditional; risk of net-negative from graph-break thrash; exploratory Medium (measure bitwise first) safe

Cheaper fully-safe alternative to hard-pinning: populate GPU_PRODUCT/NODE_NAME in the registry (schema fields exist at registry.py:332-333, but no downward-API injection was found in the job spec) so node-type becomes a recorded covariate.

docs.title: Data / IO
docs.text: Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Store chunked token cache as uint16, not int64 (vocab 50004 < 65536) Storage: certain 4x smaller cache + 4x smaller stage-to-local copies. Wall-clock: marginal (~1–3% on lstm/gpt2_small on slow nodes only; ~0 on compute-bound archs; blended <1–2%) Low (one-time prep re-run) safe Copy chunked cache to node-local emptyDir at pod init ~0–2% overall, concentrated on lstm + epoch-1 cold reads / page-cache-evicted reads on busy shared nodes; ~0% on compute-bound archs. ~5s one-time copy Low (emptyDir pattern already used) safe Raise CPU to 4 / set num_workers + persistent_workers explicitly Arch-specific; ~0% for compute-bound, low-single-digit % on lstm/gpt2_small/medium IF data_fraction shows a stall; persistent_workers saves per-epoch fork/mmap-reopen regardless Low (gate on telemetry + webhook) safe VERIFIED: no HF .shuffle() indices-indirection penalty exists 0 (documents a non-issue; prevents wasted investigation) None safe VERIFIED: drop_last=False is consistent with the checkpoint schedule 0 (informational; changing it would desync LOCKED anchors — do not) None safe

docs.title: Loop / Precision
docs.text:
Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Disable gradient checkpointing — GPT-2 family ONLY ~25% per-step on gpt2_small/medium/large; gpt2_large dominates (~60–70 GPU-h/run). Mamba/BERT yield 0 (GC already a no-op) Low safe Enable torch.compile / Inductor (compile_mode null everywhere; the line-198 dynamo.disable is a no-op, not a blocker) ~8–18% per-step on compute-bound transformers; LSTM ~0%, Mamba uncertain (verify "compilation successful" fires) Low (config flip only) safe* Switch fp16+GradScaler → bf16 (no scaler) <1% steady-state wall-clock; real value is operational (zero scaler step-skips, simpler resume) Medium (plumb dtype) needs_resweep LSTM forward: skip the per-micro-batch attention_mask.sum(dim=1).cpu() sync (chunks are unpadded, packing branch is dead) ~1–3% of LSTM step time (LSTM-only; whole-matrix <1%) Low (guard on .all() / omit mask) safe Async analysis-only checkpoint writes + drop per-save empty_cache() ~0.1–0.7% per run (best gpt2_medium ~0.4–0.7%; gpt2_large/bert ~0.05–0.24%). True volume ~39/111/106/115/241 GB for small/medium/bert/mamba/large Medium safe

*The verifier confirmed safe for the cross-cutting compile finding (pure kernel fusion under fixed fp16+GradScaler, applied uniformly from reset); the per-arch lanes flagged a needs_resweep caveat pending a 1-seed parity check. Recommend treating compile as needs-parity-validation before matrix commit.

docs.title: Cluster
docs.text: Title Verified gain Effort science_impact Raise per-cell parallelism 2 → 4–6 for light archs (lstm, gpt2_small/medium, mamba) Per-cell ceiling ~2.5x drain (5 waves → 2); end-to-end single-digit-days tail reduction, bounded by slowest pod; does NOT trip the NRP webhook Low (live-mutable / --parallelism) safe Stratify off L4 (soft-prefer fast cards) for non-LSTM archs Per L4-bound run up to ~3x faster; matrix wall-clock low-single-digit % (runs are independent — no paired-cell gating) Low design_decision 48GB open tier (A40/L40/L40S/A6000) as no-paperwork A100 fallback for gpt2_large + mamba ~5–20% per run (NOT ~50% — compute-bound at 98–100% SM, so doubling phys saves only launch overhead + escapes L4 tail) Medium (per-request-key job variants) safe

docs.title: 4. Refuted — Do NOT Do
docs.text:
• gpt2_small disable gradient checkpointing — refuted as tagged: mis-tagged safe (dropout RNG stream diverges GC-on vs GC-off → trajectory change, so needs_resweep/design_decision); aggregate gain ~6x overstated (40 runs, not 240); VRAM-safety at phys=16-GC-off on the densest ablation corpus is unverified.
  • gpt2_small enable torch.compile — refuted as written: leaves GC ON (graph breaks gut Inductor) and misreads line-198 as a blocker; realistic net ~0–1.1x as proposed.
  • gpt2_small raise phys 16→32 — ~0–3% at 98–100% SM (compute-bound); route (a) OOM-risky, route (b) depends on an unverified sibling change.
  • gpt2_small persistent_workers / CPU bump — ~0–0.2%; SM 98–100% rules out a data-bound regime; CPU bump risks the NRP webhook.
  • gpt2_small fp16→bf16 — <1%; gain overstated ~5–10x; GPU is SM-bound.
  • gpt2_large raise phys 4→16 at constant eff batch — ~1.00x standalone at 98–100% SM; phys=16 VRAM-fit is unverified and contradicted by the config's own 24GB sizing note (phys was deliberately dropped 16→4).
  • gpt2_large drop cuDNN deterministic mode — ~1.00x; cuDNN flags do not touch the cuBLAS matmuls or flash-attn kernels that dominate a transformer; no conv ops to autotune.
  • bert_large enable torch.compile (as a standalone) — refuted on its "two stacked defeaters" premise (the dynamo.disable is a no-op, not a second blocker); the real lever survives via the §3 cross-cutting compile finding at ~5–12% conditional on GC.
  • bert_large raise phys 4→8 — ~0–3%; the "~10 GB free" headroom premise is false (production runs use_gradient_checkpointing: true, so the assumed activation budget does not hold); BERT uses SDPA not FA2.
  • bert_large fp16→bf16 — ~0% (<0.1%); GradScaler sync is ~0.006% of a ~35 s step; robustness change mislabeled as throughput.
  • bert_large async checkpoint writes — gain overstated ~15–30x (~0.1–0.2%, not 3–6%); internally inconsistent with its own 200 MB/s assumption. (Note: the §3 loop/precision async-checkpoint finding IS confirmed at ~0.1–0.7%; adopt that framing, not this one's headline.)
  • lstm fp16→bf16 — negligible; assumed 1–2% overflow rate is ~10–20x too high (steady-state <0.1%); the repo's own overflow counter is dead code (never incremented).
  • lstm raise phys 16→64 — OOMs on every pool; phys 32 already hits ~87% VRAM (the logits/CE over a 50004 vocab dominate, not the recurrent core); A4000/MIG are tighter still.
  • mamba raise phys 4→16 — OOMs; resident is ~9 GB (fp32 master weights, ~558M real params) + ~24 GB activations at phys 16 (GC is a no-op, so activations are at max); only phys 4→8 fits, yielding ~2–5%, not the claimed 8–15%.
  • mamba CPU bump for >1 dataloader worker — ~0%; SM 98–100% (compute-bound), pre-chunked ~32KB batches are hidden by prefetch; phys→16 compounding doesn't apply (Mamba locked at phys 4); CPU bump risks the webhook.
  • A100 "no reservation needed, 84 open GPUs" — refuted as a live-cluster claim that contradicts repo ground truth and the task's stated facts (A100 is reservation-gated); acting on a wrong "no gate" reading is a policy violation. The A100 routing direction is real but must be gated on admin confirmation (see §2 gpt2_large).
  • Exclude L4 fleet-wide (28% of cells run 3x slower) — refuted: based on a false 2-pod-lockstep-cell model. Cells are 10-completion / parallelism-2 Indexed Jobs with independent runs and no barrier, so a slow L4 delays only its own run. Real benefit is a low-single-digit % tail trim (captured by the soft-prefer stratification instead).
  • Pin both seeds of a cell to the same GPU product — refuted: the 2-seed-pod gating mechanism does not exist; as specified (pin to an unspecified product) it risks NET SLOWDOWN by pinning all 10 runs onto slow L4 and shrinking the schedulable set ~4x. Collapses into the L4-stratification move.
  • wandb.log every step / log_metrics_every_n_steps dead field — refuted as a wall-clock win (<0.1%); the actual per-step sync is the unconditional _mean_loss().item() in the progress bar, which this fix does not touch; wandb.log is async. Worth doing only as dead-config cleanup + wandb rate-limit hygiene.
  • pin_memory=True commentary — no-op by the finder's own admission (already enabled and correct); nothing to apply.

docs.title: 5. Recommended Adoption Bundle for the Clean Re-Run
(a) Safe — adopt now (zero science impact)
docs.text:
1. Disable gradient checkpointing on the GPT-2 family only (gpt2_small carries a trajectory caveat from dropout RNG — see (b); gpt2_medium and gpt2_large are clean safe). Mamba/BERT: just remove the dead flag (honesty fix, 0 gain). — largest safe lever, gpt2_large dominant.
  2. Store the chunked token cache as uint16 — certain 4x storage/copy reduction, one-time prep re-run. Marginal wall-clock but unconditional infra win.
  3. Copy chunked cache to node-local emptyDir at pod init — ~0–2%, robustness floor on shared nodes.
  4. Async analysis-only checkpoint writes + drop per-save empty_cache() — ~0.1–0.7%, math-identical.
  5. LSTM: avoid the redundant contiguous() logits copy (pre-projection slice) — ~1–3% LSTM.
  6. LSTM: skip the dead attention_mask .cpu() sync — ~1–3% LSTM.
  7. Raise per-cell parallelism 2 → 4–6 for light archs — single-digit-days calendar tail reduction, zero GPU-days.
  8. persistent_workers=True (harmless cleanup); CPU bump only if timing/data_fraction telemetry proves a stall.

docs.title: (b) needs_resweep — decide before sweeps are frozen
docs.text:
1. torch.compile / Inductor matrix-wide — ~8–18% on the transformer subset. Mechanically a safe kernel-fusion change, but commit only after a 1-seed loss-curve parity check vs eager. Decide before sweeps so winners are validated under the same compile setting that production uses.
  2. fp16 → bf16 AMP — throughput gain is ~0 (all archs are SM-bound), but it changes the trajectory and removes loss-scaling fragility. If adopted, the HP sweeps MUST be run in bf16 too. Decision is robustness-driven, not speed-driven.
  3. gpt2_small gradient-checkpointing removal — because dropout RNG-stream divergence makes it a trajectory change, treat it as a sweep-time decision, not a free safe flip.

docs.title: (c) design_decision — PI must choose
docs.text:
1. Route gpt2_large + bert_large to A100-80GB — the single largest per-run lever (~3–4x), but GATED on confirming admin-granted nautilus.io/reservation access (repo says reservation-gated; do not tolerate unauthorized values). Falls back to the 48GB open tier (~5–20%) if A100 access fails a test pod.
  2. Per-arch GPU pool stratification (soft-prefer fast cards off L4) for the heavy/long-pole and high-step-rate archs — shifts the seed-vs-node confound the registry tracks. Prefer soft preferredDuringScheduling weighting over hard exclusion to preserve pool breadth.
  3. Move LSTM to A4000/MIG — frees 24GB slots for transformers; changes which hardware tier the LSTM confound lives on.

docs.title: Estimated combined wall-clock reduction of bundle (a) on the 300-run matrix at 60-GPU steady parallelism
docs.text:
The dominant term is gradient-checkpointing removal on the GPT-2 family. The matrix is heavily weighted toward the heavy GPT-2 cells: gpt2_large at ~5.73 GPU-days/run × ~50 runs ≈ 286 GPU-days, gpt2_medium ~21 GPU-days-equivalent × ~50, gpt2_small ~50 runs. Bundle (a) saves:

  • GPT-2 family GC removal: ~25% on ~all GPT-2 cells. gpt2_large alone: ~50 runs × ~1.2 GPU-days saved ≈ ~60 GPU-days. gpt2_medium: ~50 × ~0.25 GPU-day ≈ ~12 GPU-days. gpt2_small: small. Subtotal ≈ ~75–80 GPU-days.
  • Parallelism bump: reduces calendar makespan, not GPU-days — at 60-GPU steady parallelism it mainly shortens the tail (single-digit calendar days), so it does not add to the GPU-day total but shortens wall-clock-to-completion.
  • LSTM loop fixes (~2–6% combined on ~40–50 lstm runs of ~9h): ~few GPU-hours total.
  • Async checkpoints + uint16 + node-local copy: sub-1% each, blended ~a few GPU-days across the matrix (concentrated on light/fast archs and shared-node contention).

Net bundle (a): roughly 80–95 GPU-days saved on the 300-run matrix, overwhelmingly from gpt2_large gradient-checkpointing removal. At 60-GPU steady parallelism (~5,160 GPU-hours/day capacity), that is on the order of ~0.4–0.45 days of calendar time recovered from GPU-day reduction alone, plus an additional single-digit-days tail reduction from the parallelism bump. The big multiplicative wins (A100 routing, ~295–390 GPU-days) live in bundle (c) and require PI/admin sign-off before they can be banked.

Relevant files: /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/scripts/launch_production_training.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/scripts/production_agent.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/model_foundry/training/loop.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/model_foundry/trainer.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/model_foundry/architectures/{rnn,mamba,bert,gpt}.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/model_foundry/data.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/model_foundry/checkpoint_schedule.py, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/configs/sweeps/baselines/*_en.yaml, /Users/thomasmorton/multi-model-foundry-subject-rearing/data/sweep_winners/*_en.json.

docs.title: Replicability and Determinism Audit
docs.text:
Date: 2026-06-04

36-agent adversarially-verified audit; 24 findings confirmed / 7 refuted.

Adopted items are tracked in docs/design_ledger.md.

docs.title: Replicability and Determinism Audit — Clean Re-run of the 300-Run Subject-Drop Study
docs.text: Prepared for PI review ahead of the clean (arch × condition × HP × seed) re-run. Findings are de-duplicated across five auditors; refuted findings appear in §5. Where finders and verifiers disagreed, the verifier prevails.

docs.title: 1. Replicability scorecard
docs.text: Goal Status One-line reason G1 — bit-reproducible from (config, seed) on the same GPU BROKEN (honest fallback: per-kernel statistical replication) torch.use_deterministic_algorithms is never called and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG is never set; FA2 backward (atomicAdd), fused AdamW, TF32, and the Mamba selective-scan kernels are all run-to-run nondeterministic even on a fixed GPU. The code prints "deterministic cuDNN for reproducibility" (trainer.py:156), overstating the guarantee. G2 — killed/restarted run reproduces the uninterrupted trajectory BROKEN (silent) On resume the loop re-enters the saved epoch at batch 0 with no within-epoch fast-forward (loop.py:180,209) and re-draws the shuffle permutation from the restored mid-epoch RNG state; mid-epoch resume is the norm (almost no resume anchor lands on an epoch boundary). The pre-crash slice is trained twice on a different order and the tail is truncated. This is the load-bearing assumption the recovery design ("re-save early checkpoints assuming byte-stable trajectories") violates. G3 — same (arch, seed) shares identical init weights across the 5 conditions HOLDS-BY-ACCIDENT set_seed runs before model init and nothing between them consumes torch RNG today (_sync_vocab_size only reads len(tokenizer)), so init is condition-invariant — but it is unasserted, has no guarding test, and any future RNG consumer inserted before _initialize_model would silently break the paired design. G4 — re-runnable years later (env/image/dep/data provenance pinned) PARTIAL Source commit is recorded and core training deps are exact-pinned, but: pods run the mutable :latest image tag (recorded verbatim, no digest), clone --branch=main floating tip, several non-training deps + the Dockerfile extras block + the CUDA base image are range/tag-pinned, the cache key hashes the corpus path not its content, and the GPU model is never recorded per run. G5 — bitwise identity across GPU models ACCEPTED BY DESIGN (non-goal) Runs land on a heterogeneous 3090/A10/L4/4090 pool; cross-GPU is statistical replication only. Document as a methods-section limitation, not a bug. TF32 widens cross-GPU divergence (§3) but this is expected.

docs.title: 2. Critical findings (G2 breaks — these block the clean re-run)
docs.text: The three critical findings below all share one root cause (the DataLoader has no dedicated, epoch-keyed RNG and resume does not fast-forward) plus one amplifier (kernel nondeterminism makes even fresh restarts non-byte-identical). They must be fixed together; the RNG redesign in §4 is the unifying fix.

docs.title: C1. Resume re-runs the in-progress epoch from batch 0 with a fresh, wrongly-seeded shuffle (no fast-forward)
docs.text:
• Mechanism. load_checkpoint restores global_step and epoch only (checkpointing.py:322-323); training_state.pt stores no within-epoch batch index (checkpointing.py:127-141). The loop does for epoch in range(self.epoch, …) (loop.py:180) and builds a fresh data_iter = iter(self.dataloader) (loop.py:209) at the top of every epoch. The inner while True (loop.py:211-219) breaks only on StopIteration or global_step >= train_steps — there is no skip of consumed micro-batches. So a checkpoint saved mid-epoch E (stored as epoch=E, global_step=S) resumes by re-entering epoch E at batch 0, retraining the pre-crash slice, and then terminating ~one partial epoch early because global_step keeps climbing from S to train_steps.
  • Compounding. The re-entered epoch is not even the same permutation: data.py:447-456 is DataLoader(shuffle=True) with no generator=, so RandomSampler draws its permutation from the global torch CPU RNG at iter() time. On resume that RNG is restored to the mid-epoch save state (checkpointing.py:330-334), which differs from the state at the original epoch's start. The resumed epoch therefore trains a different data order than the uninterrupted run ever saw.
  • Why it fires routinely. With ~97 anchors over 30 epochs and front-loaded log-spaced anchors (0,1,2,4,8,…) over ~128k chunks, almost no resume-capable anchor lands on an epoch boundary, and pods are preempted often. Verifier confirmed via the schedule that of the 19 resume-state anchors, 17 happen to be exact epoch boundaries but the 2 earliest mid-epoch ones (ep7 waypoint, midpoint) plus a 1-optimizer-step rewind at boundary anchors still diverge.
  • Evidence. loop.py:115-116,180,184,209,211-219; checkpointing.py:127-141,322-334; trainer.py:439,470-475,521-526; data.py:447-456.
  • Fix. (a) Deterministic per-(seed, epoch) DataLoader generator (see §4) so the re-entered epoch's order is reproducible from epoch start; and (b) fast-forward the first resumed epoch by the restored within-epoch offset, or restrict resume-state checkpoints to epoch boundaries only. Persist an explicit within-epoch micro-batch index in training_state.pt (additive, back-compatible: old checkpoints default to 0 = legacy behavior) rather than recomputing (global_step % steps_per_epoch)*grad_accum, because the per-epoch optimizer-step count is floor-not-ceil (trailing micro-batches that never reach an accumulation boundary drop without a step, loop.py:416/441), so the modulo arithmetic can be off by a step.
  • Tradeoffs. Fast-forward costs I/O-only wall-time (up to ~one epoch of next() calls, no compute) — acceptable versus a wrong trajectory. Epoch-boundary-only resume is simpler but discards the early/mid waypoints' restartability. Pre-fix checkpoints cannot be made byte-exact retroactively — state this in methods.

docs.title: C2. Fresh-restart "deterministic overwrite" of early checkpoints is NOT byte-identical (FA2 atomicAdd backward)
docs.text:
• Mechanism. production_agent.py:278-282,304-308 restarts a pre-waypoint run from step 0 and re-saves the early weights-only anchors, asserting "the same seed re-walks the same trajectory and overwrites the same anchors." This holds only for checkpoint-0 (saved before any optimizer step — pure set_seed init). For any step>0 anchor it is false: FA2 is hard-coded (trainer.py:205), its backward accumulates dQ/dK/dV via fp32 atomicAdd (run-to-run nondeterministic on the same GPU), fused AdamW (trainer.py:298-300) and the AMP GradScaler (loop.py:74) add more, and nothing sets torch.use_deterministic_algorithms (zero matches repo-wide). After hundreds of nondeterministic backward passes the re-walked checkpoint-512 differs in the low bits.
  • False confidence. The one validated restart was on the LSTM, which does not route through FA2 attention — i.e. the one arch where the bug doesn't bite. GPT-2/BERT (the attention archs) were never exercised on this path.
  • Evidence. production_agent.py:278-282,304-308; trainer.py:153-154,205,298-300; loop.py:74; utils.py:27-34; repo-wide grep (zero use_deterministic_algorithms/CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG).
  • Fix. Recommended (A): document that fresh-restart overwrite is byte-identical only for checkpoint-0 and statistically equivalent (not bitwise) for step>0 anchors; gate the overwrite so it never overwrites a step>0 anchor a resume could already have consumed (the existing stale_steps[-1] < first_resume_anchor guard at production_agent.py:295 already enforces this — extend the comment). Option (B) (true determinism — use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True), CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, leave FA2 for SDPA) is materially slower and would undercut the FA2-motivated GPU pool. Note: transformers 4.41.2 does not plumb flash-attn's deterministic= kwarg, so "make FA2 deterministic" is not available without leaving FA2.
  • Tradeoffs. (A) is documentation-only and safe; it accepts that early overwritten anchors are statistical, not bitwise — fine because they are weights-only (no resume consumes them past the guard). (B) costs ~10–30% throughput and a GPU-pool rethink.

docs.title: C3. BERT MLM masking RNG is not restored on resume (worker-process stream)
docs.text:
• Mechanism. MaskedLMDataCollator._mask_tokens (data_collators.py:204,211,217,221) calls torch.bernoulli/torch.randint with no explicit generator, so masking draws from the ambient torch RNG of the worker process. On the production pods num_workers auto-resolves to ≥1 (data.py:434-441), so the collator runs in a worker seeded by _worker_init_fn from torch.initial_seed() (data.py:40-43). Workers are non-persistent (persistent_workers unset → respawn every epoch). training_state.pt restores only main-process RNG (checkpointing.py:330-334) — the worker base seed it depends on is re-derived from the (restored, mid-epoch) main stream, which does not match what the uninterrupted run's epoch would have used. A resumed BERT run therefore produces a different (chunk → mask) pairing for the remainder of training, silently. This is a separate stream from C1's shuffle: fixing the sampler generator does not fix the collator.
  • Scope correction. This is BERT-only (one of the five archs). The auditor's broader claim that CausalLM data order also breaks through the worker mechanism is refuted — shuffle runs in the main process and its RNG is restored (see §5). Severity downgraded from "critical, all-arch" to critical for BERT, scoped.
  • Evidence. data_collators.py:204,211,217,221; data.py:40-43,434-441,447-456; checkpointing.py:330-334; production_agent.py:313-338 (resume path applies to BERT). Note CausalLM collator (data_collators.py:165-169) uses no RNG at all.
  • Fix. Give MaskedLMDataCollator an explicit torch.Generator seeded from a stable function of (random_seed, epoch, batch_index) and pass generator=g to every bernoulli/randint. Thread epoch in via a settable attribute updated in loop.py before each iter(); use a monotonic batch counter. These are CPU ops on CPU tensors, so a CPU generator suffices (no CUDA-determinism entanglement). See §4.
  • Tradeoffs. A few lines of plumbing; no throughput cost. Do not use Python's builtin hash((seed,epoch,batch)) — it is PYTHONHASHSEED-salted per process and PYTHONHASHSEED is never set, so it would itself be nondeterministic; use seed*K + epoch*K2 + batch or hashlib.

docs.title: 3. Moderate findings (G1 / G4)
docs.text: Title Mechanism Fix Cost No use_deterministic_algorithms / CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG (G1) cudnn.deterministic=True (trainer.py:153-154) covers only cuDNN conv/RNN, not cuBLAS GEMMs (need CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 on CUDA≥10.2) or atomicAdd scatter/embedding/cross-entropy backward. Neither the API nor the env var appears anywhere. Add a training.deterministic flag (default false). When set: export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 pre-CUDA-init (bake into pod env), call torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True). Keep default-false runs byte-identical to current. ~5–15% (GEMM); 2–3× on affected scatter/embedding backward (small fraction of step). FA2 2.7.4 backward nondeterministic (G1) attn_implementation="flash_attention_2" hard-coded (trainer.py:205, wired via gpt.py:204-210) for all GPT-2; dQ accumulated via fp32 atomicAdd; transformers 4.41.2 exposes no deterministic kwarg. For a bit-repro verification subset, force attn_implementation="sdpa" when training.deterministic is set (requires use_deterministic_algorithms to also avoid SDPA's mem-efficient backward). Otherwise document GPT-2 as statistical-only. SDPA ~1.3–1.8× slower at seq_len 1000 (verification subset only). mamba-ssm 2.3.0 selective-scan / causal-conv1d backward (G1) mamba.py:180-189 uses the fused MambaSSM mixer (GPU path) with no determinism kwarg; selective-scan backward over seq_len 1000 uses parallel-scan reductions invisible to use_deterministic_algorithms (custom CUDA ext). No clean kernel fix in 2.3.0. Document Mamba as statistical-only. use_fast=False routes to the pure-PyTorch block but that is a different, slower model, not a bitwise match. Documentation; use_fast=False is 10–50× slower and numerically different. TF32 enabled in every production config (G1, also worsens G5) use_tf32: true everywhere; trainer.py:267-270 sets allow_tf32=True. Truncates the fp32 mantissa to 10 bits, amplifying low-bit nondeterminism and cross-GPU divergence. (Note: heavy GEMMs run under fp16 autocast already, so amplification is real but smaller than stated.) Under training.deterministic, force use_tf32=False. A verification run intended to bit-match a production run must use the same TF32 setting as production. TF32-off ~1.5–2× slower on Ampere matmul-bound steps (verification only). AMP GradScaler second-order trajectory fork (G2, conditional) GradScaler skip-on-overflow (loop.py:418-432) depends on exact gradient values, which are nondeterministic per the kernel findings. A divergent overflow decision = a whole missed/applied optimizer step, converting soft low-bit noise into a hard trajectory fork (and the LR scheduler advances unconditionally even on a skipped step, loop.py:432). Downstream of the kernel findings — resolves once first-order nondeterminism is removed for byte-stable runs. As a detectability mitigation, log per-step scale factor + "step skipped" events to the registry/WandB so divergence is observable. Logging only; no state change. G3 paired-init is accidental, not asserted (G3/hygiene) set_seed precedes _initialize_model and nothing between them consumes torch RNG today — but unasserted, untested. set_seed also omits PYTHONHASHSEED. Re-seed set_seed(config.random_seed) immediately before _initialize_model (trainer.py:455) to make condition-invariance structural; add a test that builds the same (arch, seed) under two conditions and asserts bitwise-equal initial state_dict. Set PYTHONHASHSEED in the pod env (not at runtime — Python fixes hash randomization at interpreter start). Do not blanket-enable use_deterministic_algorithms(True) here (would break the FA2/fused-AdamW path unless warn_only=True). Negligible (one seed call + one test). Docker image is mutable :latest, recorded verbatim (G4) Production/sweep YAMLs use :latest + imagePullPolicy: Always (launch_production_training.py:225-226); DOCKER_IMAGE env is the :latest string (:289), stored unchanged into the registry (cli.py:413 → registry.py:363). CI rebuilds :latest on every relevant push and also publishes :$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA; CI header itself says to pin the SHA. Resolve :latest → @sha256:<digest> (or use the :<short-sha> CI already emits) once at launch; stamp into both the pod spec image: and DOCKER_IMAGE; record a new docker_image_digest registry field. Pin the unpinned Dockerfile extras block and the nvidia/cuda:12.1.1 base image by digest. One registry/manifest call per launch batch. Code is cloned-at-init separately, so pinning the image does not block code iteration. Pods clone --branch=main floating tip (G4) Init container clones --single-branch --depth=1 --branch=main (launch_production_training.py:215-216); a mid-wave git push silently splits the wave across commits (8 commits to main on the recovery day alone, one touching the restart guard). Commit is recorded (cli.py:410) but not enforced. Resolve git rev-parse HEAD (or accept --git-ref) once at launch; clone that SHA in the init container (the SHA-checkout path already exists in docker-entrypoint.sh:36-41 but is currently dead code in prod); inject as GIT_REF so all pods share one code state. Trivial. A genuine mid-wave fix then requires an explicit re-pin — correct for a repro wave. Cache key hashes corpus PATH, not content (G4) cache_keys.py:92 puts os.path.abspath(corpus_path) (a string) in the payload + tokenizer bytes + seq len + manipulation — never the .train bytes. A regenerated file at the same path, or the same path on a different PVC restore, collides to the same key; the registry's recorded cache_key (registry.py:361) is path-derived, not a content fingerprint. (A sha256 of the composed corpus does exist in COMPOSE_MANIFEST.json — it is just not bound to the key or the run record.) Fold a corpus_content_hash (streamed sha256 over .train files in sorted order, or reuse the existing COMPOSE_MANIFEST checksum) into compute_cache_key's payload and into register_run_start. One streaming pass per cache build (one-shot, behind the idempotency gate); changes cache-key values (one-time recompute — fine for a clean re-run). GPU model never recorded per run (G4) Registry has gpu_product/node_name fields but cli.py:406-417 never passes them and no GPU_PRODUCT/NODE_NAME env is ever set (only nodeAffinity selectors); registry.py:381 drops the resulting Nones. The landed card survives only as free-text nvidia-smi -L in the env-snapshot sidecar. Add NODE_NAME via downward-API fieldRef: spec.nodeName to the trainer container; pass gpu_product=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) (already available via utils.get_device) and node_name into register_run_start. One line each side. Enables partition-by-GPU to verify the G5 limitation and the G1 "same GPU model" precondition. Range-pinned deps + tag-pinned base image (G4) Core training deps are exact-pinned and torch/FA2/mamba/causal-conv1d are ARG-pinned, but pyarrow>=, polars>=, boto3>=, scikit-learn>=, etc. (requirements.txt:19-38), the Dockerfile extras block (accelerate>=0.26.0, bare pandas/einops/spacy-transformers/pytest, Dockerfile:52-61), and the nvidia/cuda:12.1.1… base tag (Dockerfile:19) all re-resolve on rebuild. None sit on the training numeric path, so this is provenance, not trajectory. Exact-pin the range deps to the live-pod pip freeze; pin the extras block; pin the base image by @sha256; bake + assert a pip-freeze lockfile at build. Pins to versions already running → behaviorally neutral. Must be paired with the :latest→SHA fix to fully close the loop.

docs.title: 4. The RNG redesign (one coherent proposal)
docs.text:
The current pipeline has no dedicated RNG streams — every random consumer draws from the single global torch RNG, entangling data order, masking, and dropout with arch-specific model-init draw counts and with resume timing. Replace this with explicit, purpose-salted generators, all derived from one base seed via a stable (non-hash()) derivation.

Base derivation helper (new, e.g. model_foundry/rng.py): 

def derive_seed(base_seed, purpose, epoch=0, batch=0):
    # stable across processes/pods — NO Python builtin hash()
    h = hashlib.blake2b(f"{base_seed}|{purpose}|{epoch}|{batch}".encode(), digest_size=8)
    return int.from_bytes(h.digest(), "little") & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

Stream Derivation Purpose-salt? Arch-salt? Lands in After fix, honest claim per arch Weight init global torch RNG, seeded by set_seed(base_seed) re-called immediately before _initialize_model n/a n/a (intentionally) trainer.py:455 (move/duplicate set_seed) + new G3 test Bitwise-identical init across the 5 conditions for fixed (arch, seed) — asserted, not accidental. Kernel-independent. Data order (shuffle) g_data = torch.Generator(); g_data.manual_seed(derive_seed(base_seed, "data_order", epoch)) — reseeded each epoch, passed as generator= to the DataLoader; recreate/reseed in loop.py before each iter() yes NO (PI decision — recommend no salt) data.py:447 + loop.py:209 Data order is a pure function of (seed, epoch), restart-stable, and identical across arches at equal seed (a property the paired design wants; currently arch-dependent). MLM masking (BERT) g_mask = torch.Generator(); g_mask.manual_seed(derive_seed(base_seed, "mlm_mask", epoch, batch_idx)) passed into every bernoulli/randint yes implicit via base_seed data_collators.py:204,211,217,221 + epoch/batch threaded from loop.py Masking is reproducible, fresh-per-epoch, and independent of worker-spawn timing → restart-stable. CPU generator (CPU tensors) — no CUDA entanglement. Dropout (GPT-2 / BERT / LSTM / Mamba) CUDA philox stream, seeded by set_seed; already saved/restored in training_state.pt (checkpointing.py:330-334) n/a n/a no change needed Restart-stable already (CUDA RNG is checkpointed). Only the kernel (not the RNG) is nondeterministic — see below. Worker __getitem__ _worker_init_fn should derive from derive_seed(base_seed, "worker", epoch, worker_id) rather than torch.initial_seed() yes implicit data.py:40-45 Decoupled from the global stream; only relevant if any map-side randomness is added later (currently none).

Determinism claim each arch can honestly make after the RNG redesign alone (RNG streams fixed, kernels unchanged):

  • GPT-2 (small/medium/large): data order, masking-N/A, dropout, and init are all reproducible and restart-stable → trajectory matches on resume up to FA2 atomicAdd backward noise. Same-GPU = statistical replication (bit-repro only if training.deterministic: SDPA + use_deterministic_algorithms + TF32 off).
  • BERT large: as GPT-2, plus masking now restart-stable (closes C3). Same-GPU = statistical (SDPA backward + atomicAdd reductions).
  • LSTM: init/data/dropout reproducible; cuDNN RNG backward is on the deterministic path (cudnn.deterministic=True is set) → can credibly claim bitwise same-GPU once use_deterministic_algorithms + CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG are added and validated (cuDNN may raise for some hidden sizes — validate the cell). Does not use FA2.
  • Mamba 370M: init/data/dropout reproducible; the fused selective-scan/conv backward is nondeterministic and invisible to the determinism guard → statistical replication only, no bitwise path without switching to the (different, slower) pure-PyTorch block.

The RNG redesign is necessary but not sufficient for G2: it makes the resumed epoch's order/masks reproducible, but C1's within-epoch fast-forward (or epoch-boundary-only resume) is still required so the resumed run doesn't re-train the epoch prefix.

docs.title: 5. Refuted findings (kept here so they stay dead)
docs.text:
• GradScaler scaler-state overwrite corrupts resume — Refuted. The fresh-restart overwrite only rewrites weights-only (scaler-less) early anchors below min(resume_state_steps); no resume ever reads a scaler from an overwritten anchor (guarded at production_agent.py:295). Already-enforced invariant, not a defect.
  • Worker RNG makes every epoch use the SAME shuffle/mask pattern — Refuted. Misreads PyTorch: with persistent_workers=False, each epoch's iter() draws a NEW base_seed from the main global RNG, so torch.initial_seed() in the worker differs every epoch; masks already vary per epoch. Shuffle runs in the main process, not workers.
  • cuDNN LSTM backward breaks G1 now — Refuted. cudnn.deterministic=True IS set (trainer.py:154), which puts cuDNN RNN on the deterministic path — the finding concedes this mid-text. The "raises under use_deterministic_algorithms" half is hypothetical (that flag is never set) and version-unverifiable on torch 2.5.1.
  • MLM masking finding tagged critical/all-effects (data_collators #1) — Refuted as written. Its headline ("masks byte-identical across every epoch") rests on the same PyTorch misreading above; the genuine resume-only divergence is the scoped BERT break already captured in C3. Its hash()-based fix is itself nondeterministic (PYTHONHASHSEED).
  • Shuffle entangled with arch-init defeats cross-arch matched-data comparisons (data_collators #3) — Refuted as a G1 break. Its own text concedes data order is deterministic per fixed arch, so G1 is not broken; the "matched data order across arches" requirement is invented (the study requires matched tokens seen, not matched order). The real residual (entanglement fragility) is the same known shuffle finding, fixed by §4.
  • Env snapshot S3 best-effort makes outage runs un-auditable — Refuted. git_commit and config_hash are durably written to checkpoint-*/metadata.json on the same CephFS PVC as the weights (checkpointing.py:152-189), independent of S3. The only at-risk artifact is the pip-freeze manifest, itself largely recoverable from the pinned commit's requirements.txt. Residual is minor, not moderate.
  • nvidia-smi -L omits driver version, recorded nowhere — Refuted. Trainer._save_environment_snapshot (trainer.py:345-392, called at :506) writes full nvidia-smi (driver + CUDA version) and torch.version.cuda to a durable PVC-symlinked logs path. Driver provenance exists; it is just not a queryable column (covered by the GPU-model finding's promote-to-field fix).

docs.title: 6. Fix bundle for the clean re-run (ordered, smallest-diff-first)
docs.text:
1. Re-seed before model init + add G3 assertion test. Duplicate set_seed(config.random_seed) at trainer.py:455; add a test building the same (arch, seed) under two conditions asserting bitwise-equal initial state_dict. (Makes G3 structural.)
  2. Set PYTHONHASHSEED in the pod env (launcher YAML), not at runtime. (Hygiene; prerequisite for any stable tuple-hash derivation.)
  3. Pin the wave's git SHA. Launcher resolves git rev-parse HEAD once, clones that SHA (wire up the existing docker-entrypoint.sh:36-41 path), injects GIT_REF. (Unifies code state; G4.)
  4. Pin the image by digest + record it. Use the CI :<short-sha>/@sha256 in all production YAMLs and DOCKER_IMAGE; add docker_image_digest to the registry; pin Dockerfile extras + base image. Exact-pin the requirements.txt range deps to live pip freeze. (G4; behaviorally neutral.)
  5. Record GPU model per run. NODE_NAME via downward API; pass torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) + node_name into register_run_start. (G4; enables G5 partition.)
  6. Add corpus_content_hash to the cache key and run record. Reuse the COMPOSE_MANIFEST sha256 or stream .train bytes. (G4; one-time cache recompute.)
  7. RNG redesign — dedicated generators (§4): per-(seed, epoch) DataLoader generator (data.py:447 + loop.py:209) and per-(seed, epoch, batch) MLM-collator generator (data_collators.py). (Closes the cross-arch entanglement and is the prerequisite for resume determinism.)
  8. Resume fast-forward + within-epoch index in training_state.pt (C1): persist the micro-batch position; on resume, advance the first epoch's iterator by that offset (or restrict resume-state anchors to epoch boundaries). Additive, back-compatible (old checkpoints → offset 0). (Closes the G2 silent break.)
  9. Add a training.deterministic path (default false): CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 + torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True) + use_tf32=False + force SDPA. Validate per-arch (LSTM cuDNN may raise). Use for the bit-repro verification subset only. (Gives an honest bitwise claim where the kernels allow it; production stays speed-first.)
  10. Correct the overstated print + log scaler events. Change trainer.py:156 to state the real (per-kernel) guarantee; log per-step GradScaler scale + skip events to the registry so trajectory divergence is detectable.

NOT fixed — accepted limitations for the methods section:

  • G1 is statistical, not bitwise, for the production wave on GPT-2/BERT/Mamba: FA2 atomicAdd backward, fused AdamW, fp16 AMP, TF32, and Mamba's fused selective-scan are nondeterministic even on the same GPU. Bitwise same-GPU repro is available only for the training.deterministic verification subset (and, for LSTM, possibly the full path).
  • G5 cross-GPU is non-goal: heterogeneous 3090/A10/L4/4090 pool; TF32 and differing tensor-core layouts/driver versions make cross-GPU bit-identity impossible. Document as statistical replication.
  • Pre-fix checkpoints cannot be made byte-exact retroactively; only the clean re-run gets the fixed trajectory. These changes alter trajectories versus any in-flight training_state.pt, so apply them only to the clean wave, never mid-study.
  • Fresh-restart overwrite of step>0 weights-only anchors is statistically equivalent, not byte-identical, unless the verification-subset determinism path is used — the recovery design's "byte-stable" framing is corrected accordingly.

docs.title: Corpus Analysis
docs.text: Sentence-level linguistic annotation and analysis pipeline for multi-genre English and Italian corpora. Processes raw text through spaCy, extracts syntactic phenomena (null subjects, that-trace contexts, expletives, wh-extraction, etc.), and writes structured Parquet output for downstream querying and statistical analysis.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Annotate a corpus split
python -m analysis.corpus_descriptives.run \
  --config configs/analysis/corpus/corpus_analysis_train90m.yaml \
  --annotate

# Run aggregate analyses over annotated data
python -m analysis.corpus_descriptives.run \
  --config configs/analysis/corpus/corpus_analysis_train90m.yaml

# Query annotations
from analysis.corpus_descriptives.query import AnnotatedCorpus

corpus = AnnotatedCorpus("data/output/train_90M/annotated_corpus/train_90M.parquet")
null_subj = corpus.get_null_subject_sentences(genre="CHILDES_child")

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
The pipeline has two modes:

  1. Annotation mode (--annotate) — Runs 12 annotators over each sentence and writes per-sentence Parquet files. This is the primary mode for producing data.
  2. Analyzer mode (default) — Runs 8 analyzers that accumulate genre-stratified counts. Outputs JSON and CSV summaries. Useful for quick corpus statistics without preserving sentence-level detail.

Both modes share the same spaCy frontend, config format, and line-cleaning infrastructure.
